blocks.content: Computer networking is the practice of connecting computers and other devices together to share resources, exchange data, and communicate. Networks allow computers to share files, printers, internet connections, and other resources efficiently.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Local Area Networks (LAN) cover limited geographical areas like offices or homes, offering high data transfer speeds.
Metropolitan Area Networks (MAN) connect users across larger regions such as an entire city.
Wide Area Networks (WAN) span vast geographical distances, combining multiple LANs across countries or continents.
Network devices perform distinct roles: Hubs broadcast data to all ports, Switches forward data selectively, and Routers connect disparate networks.
Network topology defines the structural layout of connections, including Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, and Tree configurations.

blocks.content: A computer network is a group of interconnected computers and devices that communicate with each other using communication channels. Networking allows users to share data, hardware devices, and software applications.

items: Resource sharing (printers, storage devices).
Data sharing between users.
Communication through email and messaging.
Centralized management of data.
Improved reliability and backup systems.

cells: Covers a small geographical area such as a home, office, or school.
Covers a large geographical area such as countries or continents.

blocks.content: A Local Area Network connects computers within a limited area such as a building, office, or school. LANs provide high data transfer speed and are commonly used in organizations.
A Metropolitan Area Network covers a larger geographical area than LAN, typically a city. It connects multiple LANs within a metropolitan region.
A Wide Area Network connects computers over very large distances such as across countries or continents. The Internet is the largest example of WAN.
A Computer Network connects independent computers to enable resource sharing, data transfer, and communication across various geographical distances.

cells: Connects multiple networks and directs data packets between them.
Connects devices within a LAN and forwards data to the correct device.
Basic networking device that broadcasts data to all connected devices.
Converts digital signals into analog signals and vice versa for internet communication.

blocks.content: A router is a networking device that forwards data packets between different networks. It determines the best path for data to travel.
A switch connects multiple devices in a LAN and sends data only to the intended device, improving network efficiency.
A hub is a simple networking device that connects multiple computers in a network and broadcasts incoming data to all connected devices.
A modem (Modulator-Demodulator) converts digital signals from a computer into analog signals for transmission over telephone lines and vice versa.

cells: All devices share a single communication line.
All devices are connected to a central hub or switch.
Devices are connected in a circular path.
Each device connects to multiple other devices.

blocks.content: In a bus topology, all computers are connected to a single communication cable called the backbone.
In star topology, all devices are connected to a central device such as a hub or switch.

items: Hub vs. Switch: Hubs operate at the Physical Layer (Layer 1) and broadcast data, while Switches operate at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) and send unicast frame traffic.
Mesh Topology Formula: The total number of cables required in a fully connected mesh network with 'n' devices is n(n-1)/2.
Modem Function: Modem stands for Modulator-Demodulator; it converts digital computer signals to analog signals for transmission over telephone lines and vice versa.

blocks.content: In ring topology, each device is connected to two other devices forming a circular network.
In mesh topology, every device is connected to every other device in the network.
Tree topology combines characteristics of star and bus topologies forming a hierarchical network.
